A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DIF research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–G are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on three simulated ODE systems, including prediction comparisons, ablations, symbolic regression, sensitivity analyses, and implementation timings.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendices F–G, including analyses moved from the earlier appendix into the main text.

M1.justification: The transformer encoder, invariant/environment embeddings, hypernetwork decoder, adversarial objective, derivative-fitting procedure, and reference-based implementation are unchanged. The added baseline descriptions do not revise DIF.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ME-Pendulum, ME-Lotka-Volterra, and ME-SIREpidemic with the same environments. Newly discussed graph-structured systems are future directions, not additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: MAML, CoDA, IRM, and VREx remain the comparison methods in Figure 4 and Table 7. Table 8 retains the same implementation comparators. New Appendix E.1.1 documents existing baseline adaptations.

E3.justification: The 800/200 training/test splits, batch size 32, 2,000 training epochs, NRMSE metric, hyperparameter searches, and sensitivity-study settings are retained. Appendix E.1.1 supplies additional descriptions without reporting changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same full-versus-invariant comparisons, component ablations, input-length and environment-count analyses, symbolic explanations, and trajectory visualizations. V1 Appendix F.1–F.2 becomes v2 Sections 5.5–5.6 without new analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Reporting remains unchanged: distributions across sampled hyperparameter configurations and timing means with standard deviations from the same 200-iteration benchmark. No new seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests appear.

E6.justification: Numerical results, symbolic expressions, and plotted findings are retained. V1 Table 6 becomes v2 Table 2 with identical invariant-trajectory NRMSEs of 0.3561, 0.6194, and 0.0652. Tables 7–8 and the remaining result figures also match.

T1.justification: V2 adds an explicit scope qualification to Theorem 3.1: it considers any possible function h under the causal assumption rather than a specific neural-network realization. This limits how the guarantee should be understood; the theorem equations and Appendix C proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: introducing invariant function learning, a causal formulation, DIF and its learning principle, and multi-environment ODE benchmarking.

C2.justification: New Appendix B Q4 explains why separately fitted symbolic equations can obscure shared dynamics through entangled environmental effects. The limitations also newly identify high-dimensional graph-structured systems, with their noise and environmental sensitivity, as an unresolved extension.

D1.justification: New Appendix E.1.1 details baseline architectures, inputs, outputs, training, and invariant-function inference. V2's abstract reports code release through AIRS and supplies a location, whereas v1 only promises release upon acceptance. That future-release footnote nevertheless remains in v2.

R1.justification: Section 4 expands positioning against modulated neural ODEs, sparse symbolic identification, graph-structured discovery, amortized equation discovery, and mechanistic neural networks. Six cited works are added, while the central distinction of extracting invariant components across environments is retained.

P1.justification: Two appendix analyses move into Sections 5.5–5.6, the remaining appendix subsections and research questions are relabeled, and FAQ, baseline, and related-work explanations expand. Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The existing invariant-function validation table moves from Appendix Table 6 to main-text Table 2 and is reduced in display size. Appendix figures and tables are repositioned, but the same 15 figures and eight tables remain without new graphical evidence.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility documentation through explicit baseline recipes and a reported code location, strengthens research positioning, and makes existing validation evidence more accessible in the main text. These limited gains outweigh the code-release wording inconsistency. The empirical evidence and proofs themselves remain unchanged.
